specs.odorSystem: Heat-sealed waste bag + deodoriser + carbon filter

verdict: The SNOW+ heat-seals the waste bag after every cycle, and on the evidence available it is the most effective odor solution in this category — nothing else physically closes the bag. The catch is unavoidable: the sealing film is proprietary, it costs roughly $120 a year, and if PetSnowy stops making it the box becomes an ordinary one. That is the whole trade.
pros: Heat-sealed bags — the strongest odor containment available
cons: Sealing film is proprietary and mandatory at around $120 a year
Smaller effective waste capacity because of the sealing mechanism
bestFor: Households where odor is a dealbreaker
People who do not mind consumables

sections.setup: Around twenty minutes, with an extra step: loading the sealing film cartridge and running a test seal. Get that wrong and the first few cycles will not seal properly.
sections.app: Adequate. Cycle control, scheduling, a film-remaining indicator and basic logging. The film counter is the most useful thing in it, because running out mid-week is a real problem.
sections.odorControl: The best in this index, and not by a small margin. Heat-sealing the bag after every cycle removes the mechanism by which every other box eventually smells. Nothing else here physically closes the waste.
sections.noise: Around 45 dB at three feet including the sealing step, which adds a brief low hum rather than a bang. Quieter than both CATLINK models.
sections.cleaning: Good, with wide litter compatibility. The trade is capacity: the sealing mechanism eats space, so the usable drawer is 7 L against 9–11 L elsewhere, and you will empty it more often.
sections.safety: Infrared, weight sensing and anti-pinch reverse. Standard coverage. The sealing element is isolated from the cat-accessible area.
sections.consumables: Proprietary sealing film at roughly $120 a year, plus filters — the highest running cost of any box here and completely non-optional. If PetSnowy stops making the film, the box becomes an ordinary one.
sections.longTermCost: Expensive to buy and the most expensive to run. Over five years it is the second-costliest box in this index after the Purobot Ultra. You are buying the odor result and paying rent on it.
